reference.title: Fix ox prime agent-ID reuse after /clear
reference.summary: Diagnosed and partially fixed a recording-loss bug where ox agent prime, when invoked from the Claude Code /clear hook, minted a fresh agent ID instead of reusing the existing one — orphaning the active session recording. Root cause: the hook subprocess lost SAGEOX_AGENT_ID across process boundaries. The fix landed three defense-in-depth changes: explicitly pass SAGEOX_AGENT_ID into the prime subprocess, add env-var and sole-active-recording fallbacks in runAgentPrime, and finalize the old session via stopSessionForClear before the new agent takes over. 7 regression tests added; the 12,198-test suite stayed green. A second related bug — sessions in the speaker repo showing stopped_at 2-9 seconds after start — was investigated but not resolved; the leading hypothesis (cross-agent session-marker collision) is documented for follow-up.
key_actions: Traced the agent-ID regeneration path from /clear hook through prime subprocess
Passed SAGEOX_AGENT_ID through the hook-to-prime subprocess boundary
Added env-var and sole-active-recording fallbacks in runAgentPrime
Implemented stopSessionForClear to finalize the pre-/clear session
Wrote 7 regression tests covering the three defense layers
Investigated but did not resolve a second bug: premature stopped_at in the speaker repo
Documented cross-agent session-marker collision as the leading hypothesis for Bug 2
